# Control Narrative: Fire Water System (Module FW)

**Document:** CN-FW-001 Rev A (draft for review)
**Scope:** Site PLC/SCADA functions for fire pumps FP-1 and FP-2, jockey pump JP-1, and header PT-601.
**Governing codes:** NFPA 20 (pump installation and controllers), NFPA 25 (inspection, testing, impairments), NFPA 72 (supervisory signals), and the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and insurer. This system is not a SIS. IEC 61511 does not apply.

---

## 0. Corrections to the client draft

The draft gives the PLC control authority that NFPA 20 assigns to the listed fire pump controllers. The narrative below makes the PLC a **monitor-only** system.

| # | Client draft intent | Correction | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PLC starts fire pumps on low header pressure | Each listed controller starts its pump from its own pressure sensing line. PLC has no start output. PT-601 is for monitoring only. | NFPA 20: automatic start comes from the controller's own pressure-sensing device. A PLC must not be in the start path. |
| C2 | PLC stops pumps after pressure recovers for 10 minutes | PLC has no stop function. Recommended: **manual stop only**, at the controller. If the AHJ and insurer permit automatic shutdown, the controller does it with its running period timer. The minimums are 10 min for electric FP-2 and **30 min for diesel FP-1** (SP-05, SP-06). A 10-minute stop is wrong for FP-1. | NFPA 20 running period timer rules. Automatic shutdown is not allowed where the AHJ requires manual shutdown. Petrochemical sites with deluge or foam often require manual shutdown. |
| C3 | PLC trips FP-1 on low lube oil pressure and high coolant temperature | **Delete.** These conditions are alarms only. A fire pump engine must keep running and sacrifice itself. The only automatic engine shutdown is overspeed, which the engine/controller does, with manual reset at the engine. | NFPA 20 diesel engine and controller requirements. |
| C4 | PLC/SCADA as the supervisory system | Required supervisory signals go to the fire alarm control panel (FACP) per NFPA 72. PLC/SCADA is supplementary. Confirm with AHJ (OI-03). | NFPA 20 / NFPA 72 |
| C5 | Monitored signal list | Add: controller "not in AUTO" for FP-1 and FP-2. Add FP-2 power-source signals (power failure, phase reversal, on alternate source, alternate isolating switch open). Add separate FP-1 overspeed and battery/charger signals if the controller provides them. Add JP-1 run. | NFPA 20 controller alarm signals. A single "trouble" point loses the information the operator needs. |
| C6 | Start-point stagger | Accepted (10 psi steps). Jockey stop must be checked against FP churn plus suction, and against system component ratings (OI-01). | NFPA 20 Annex A setpoint guidance |

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

**FR-FW-001** The site PLC monitors, alarms, logs, and trends the fire water pump system. *Test: FAT I/O check and alarm test.*

**FR-FW-002** The site PLC has no output that starts, stops, resets, or changes the mode of FP-1, FP-2, or JP-1. *Test: I/O list review; FAT confirms no outputs are wired to these controllers.*

- **Upstream:** fire water tank/suction supply (suction pressure and tank level are not in this scope; see OI-07).
- **Downstream:** fire water ring main, hydrants, monitors, deluge and foam systems.
- **Peer systems:** FACP (required supervision), listed pump controllers (control authority), JP-1 controller.

## 2. Equipment and tags

No instrument index was given. Tags marked (P) are proposed.

| Tag | Description | Signal to PLC |
|---|---|---|
| FP-1 | Diesel fire pump, listed diesel controller | See signals below |
| FP-2 | Electric fire pump, listed electric controller with ATS | See signals below |
| JP-1 | Jockey pump, own controller and pressure switch | Run |
| PT-601 | Header pressure transmitter, 4-20 mA | AI |
| LT-610 | FP-1 fuel tank level, 4-20 mA | AI |
| TT-611 (P) | Pump room temperature, 4-20 mA | AI |
| XS-601A (P) | FP-1 engine running | DI |
| XA-601A (P) | FP-1 fail to start | DI |
| XA-601B (P) | FP-1 controller common trouble | DI |
| XA-601C (P) | FP-1 controller not in AUTO | DI |
| XA-601D (P) | FP-1 overspeed shutdown (if available) | DI |
| XA-601E (P) | FP-1 battery or charger failure (if available) | DI |
| XS-602A (P) | FP-2 pump running | DI |
| XA-602A (P) | FP-2 fail to start / power failure | DI |
| XA-602B (P) | FP-2 controller trouble / phase reversal | DI |
| XA-602C (P) | FP-2 controller not in AUTO | DI |
| XS-602D (P) | FP-2 on alternate source (ATS) | DI |
| XA-602E (P) | FP-2 alternate source isolating switch open | DI |
| XS-603A (P) | JP-1 running | DI |

**FR-FW-003** Each alarm DI uses a contact that is closed when healthy, so a wire break gives an alarm. *Test: FAT; lift each wire and confirm alarm.* (Depends on controller contact options; see OI-04.)

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

The controllers own all transitions. The PLC **infers** the state from field signals and displays it.

| State | Entry permissive / condition | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 Standby | FP-1, FP-2 in AUTO; no trouble; no pump running; PT-601 at or above SP-02 | S2, S3, S4, S5, S6 | — | Controller automatic |
| S2 Pressure maintenance | JP-1 running | S1 (header reaches SP-01, JP-1 stops), S3, S6 | JP-1 controller | Controller automatic |
| S3 Fire pump running – auto | FP-2 or FP-1 running after header falls below SP-03 or SP-04 | S1 by manual stop at controller (or controller auto-stop, SP-05/SP-06, if permitted); S6 | Fire pump controller | Controller automatic; stop manual |
| S4 Fire pump running – manual | Pump running started from controller START, remote manual station, or deluge input | S1 by manual stop at controller; S6 | Operator at controller | Manual |
| S5 Weekly test | Operator sets TEST flag on HMI before controller weekly test | S1 when operator clears flag and pumps are stopped; S6 | Operator | Manual (PLC records only) |
| S6 Impaired | Any controller not in AUTO, any trouble, fail to start, PT-601 bad, or operator impairment flag | S1 when all causes clear and operator closes impairment on HMI | Automatic (PLC detects) | PLC monitor; impairment per NFPA 25 program |

**FR-FW-010** The PLC displays the inferred state S1–S6 within SP-20 of a signal change. *Test: FAT; simulate each entry condition.*

**FR-FW-011** The PLC shows S6 whenever any S6 cause is present, regardless of other states. *Test: FAT; force each cause during S2 and S3.*

**FR-FW-012** The TEST flag does not suppress any alarm. *Test: FAT; set flag, force trouble, confirm alarm.*

## 4. Regulatory control

None in PLC scope.

- JP-1 pressure maintenance is done by the JP-1 controller between SP-02 and SP-01.
- FP-2 and FP-1 start by their controllers at SP-03 and SP-04.
- These settings are listed controller settings. They are verified at the NFPA 20 acceptance test, not at PLC FAT.

**FR-FW-020** The PLC compares PT-601 with the controller setpoints for diagnosis only. It does not act on the result. *Test: FAT review of logic.*

## 5. Sequences

The PLC runs no sequence. The table below defines the expected pressure-decay response and the PLC discrepancy checks. Use it as the FAT/SAT script.

| Step | Expected action (by controller) | PLC transition condition | Timeout | PLC failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header falls below SP-02. JP-1 starts. | XS-603A on | SP-14 | Alarm "JP-1 not running at low pressure" (A-09) |
| 2 | Header recovers to SP-01. JP-1 stops. | XS-603A off | SP-15 | Alarm "JP-1 long run – possible leak" (A-10) |
| 3 | Header falls below SP-03. FP-2 starts. | XS-602A on | SP-16 | Alarm "FP-2 not running at low pressure" (A-11) |
| 4 | Header falls below SP-04. FP-1 starts and runs the crank cycle (SP-07). | XS-601A on | SP-17 | Alarm "FP-1 not running at low pressure" (A-12) |
| 5 | Header recovers above SP-01 with a fire pump running. Pump keeps running. | Operator stops pump at controller | None (manual) | None. Pump running alarm stays active until pump stops. |

**FR-FW-030** The PLC raises each discrepancy alarm in the table when its timeout expires. *Test: FAT with simulated PT-601 and run signals.*

**FR-FW-031** The PLC never issues a command in response to a discrepancy. *Test: I/O list review.*

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No cause-and-effect chart was given. The PLC has **no interlocks**. The rows below record controller functions so that scope is clear. These are verified at the NFPA 20 acceptance test.

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Header below SP-03 at FP-2 sensing line | FP-2 starts | Latched (runs until stopped) | Manual stop at FP-2 controller (or auto-stop after SP-05 if permitted) | FP-2 controller |
| Header below SP-04 at FP-1 sensing line | FP-1 starts | Latched | Manual stop at FP-1 controller (or auto-stop after SP-06 if permitted) | FP-1 controller |
| FP-1 engine overspeed (SP-08) | FP-1 engine shuts down; alarm | Latched | Manual reset at engine, then controller | FP-1 engine/controller |
| FP-1 low lube oil pressure | **Alarm only. No shutdown.** | — | — | FP-1 controller |
| FP-1 high coolant temperature | **Alarm only. No shutdown.** | — | — | FP-1 controller |
| FP-2 normal power failure | ATS transfers to alternate source | Auto-reset (retransfer per ATS) | Automatic | FP-2 controller/ATS |
| Any PLC signal | No effect on pumps | — | — | — |

**FR-FW-040** Loss, failure, or reset of the PLC does not start, stop, or prevent the start of any pump. *Test: FAT/SAT; remove PLC power with FP-2 running and with system in S1; confirm no change and that a pressure drop still starts the pumps.*

## 7. Alarms

No rationalized alarm database was given. Priorities follow the site alarm philosophy (OI-06).

| ID | Tag | Alarm | Setpoint | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-01 | XS-601A / XS-602A | Fire pump running | — | Confirm fire event or test. Send operator to pump room. |
| A-02 | XA-601A / XA-602A | Fire pump fail to start / FP-2 power failure | — | Send operator to pump room. Start pump manually at controller. Start impairment procedure. |
| A-03 | XA-601B / XA-602B | Controller trouble | — | Investigate at controller. Read controller display for cause. |
| A-04 | XA-601C / XA-602C | Controller not in AUTO | — | Return controller to AUTO or start impairment procedure. |
| A-05 | XA-601D | FP-1 overspeed shutdown | — | Start impairment procedure. Call engine service. |
| A-06 | XA-601E | FP-1 battery or charger failure | — | Call electrical maintenance. |
| A-07 | XS-602D / XA-602E | FP-2 on alternate source / isolating switch open | — | Check normal supply. Close isolating switch. |
| A-08 | PT-601 | Header pressure low | SP-10 | Check that pumps are running. Look for line break or open hydrant. |
| A-09 | XS-603A | JP-1 not running at low pressure | SP-14 | Check JP-1 controller. |
| A-10 | XS-603A | JP-1 long run | SP-15 | Look for leak or open valve. |
| A-11 | XS-602A | FP-2 not running at low pressure | SP-16 | Start FP-2 at controller. |
| A-12 | XS-601A | FP-1 not running at low pressure | SP-17 | Start FP-1 at controller. |
| A-13 | XS-603A | JP-1 excessive starts | SP-18 | Look for leak. Check JP-1 controller settings. |
| A-14 | PT-601 | Header pressure high | SP-11 | Check relief valve. Check pump churn pressure. |
| A-15 | LT-610 | FP-1 fuel low | SP-12 | Refill fuel tank. |
| A-16 | LT-610 | FP-1 fuel refill pre-alert | SP-13 | Schedule fuel delivery. |
| A-17 | TT-611 | Pump room temperature low | SP-19 | Check room heater. |
| A-18 | TT-611 | Pump room temperature high | SP-21 | Check ventilation louvers and fans. |
| A-19 | PT-601 / LT-610 / TT-611 | Bad PV | SP-22 | Call instrument technician. |
| A-20 | PLC | Comms loss to SCADA or remote I/O | SP-20 | Send operator to pump room. Monitor at FACP and locally. |

**FR-FW-050** Each alarm activates at its setpoint and clears when the condition clears. *Test: FAT, each alarm.*

**FR-FW-051** A-13 counts JP-1 starts in a rolling one-hour window. *Test: FAT; pulse XS-603A above SP-18 starts in one hour.*

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | PLC response | Effect on pumps |
|---|---|---|
| PT-601 bad PV (outside SP-22) | A-19. Mark pressure value bad. Inhibit A-08, A-14, and step 1–4 discrepancy alarms. Enter S6. | None. Controllers use their own sensing lines. |
| LT-610 bad PV | A-19. Inhibit A-15 and A-16. | None. Operator does manual tank check each shift until repaired. |
| TT-611 bad PV | A-19. Inhibit A-17 and A-18. | None. |
| DI wire break | Alarm activates (FR-FW-003). | None. |
| SCADA/PLC comms loss | A-20 at SCADA after SP-20. Hold last value with bad quality. | None. FACP supervision continues. |
| PLC power loss | SCADA raises A-20. | None (FR-FW-040). |
| PLC restart | Read all current inputs before alarm processing. Reset JP-1 start counter to zero. Log restart event. Do not reannunciate alarms that cleared during the outage. | None. |
| Normal power loss to site | FP-2 ATS transfers. FP-1 runs on its batteries. PLC on UPS (OI-05). | Pumps start as needed by controllers. |

**Fail positions:** The PLC has no outputs to the pump system. FP-1, FP-2, and JP-1 keep their current state on any PLC failure.

**FR-FW-060** Each abnormal response in the table is demonstrated at FAT. *Test: FAT, simulate each condition.*

## 9. Operator interface

**What the operator sees:** inferred state S1–S6; PT-601 trend with SP-01 to SP-04 shown as reference lines; run and alarm status of each pump; LT-610 in percent of tank capacity; TT-611; JP-1 starts in the last hour; impairment banner.

**What the operator changes:** the TEST flag (S5) and the impairment flag (S6) only.

**Prompts:**

- On TEST flag set: "Make sure that the FACP monitoring station knows about the test. Start the test at the controller."
- On S6 entry: "Fire protection is impaired. Start the impairment procedure."

**FR-FW-070** The HMI has no START, STOP, RESET, or mode command for FP-1, FP-2, or JP-1. *Test: FAT display review.*

> **WARNING:** Do not stop a fire pump while a fire event is active. Fire water supply stops when the pump stops.

**FR-FW-071** Operations signs off states S1–S6 and the prompts before FAT. *Test: signed review record.*

## 10. Open items

| OI-05 | Confirm PLC and SCADA UPS autonomy. | Integrator | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-06 | Assign alarm priorities per site alarm philosophy. | Controls lead | 2026-11-27 |
| OI-07 | Decide whether suction pressure and fire water tank level are in this module. | Client | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-08 | Confirm whether FP-1 and FP-2 share a room. This sets SP-19. | Client | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-09 | Confirm PT-601 range, LT-610 tank geometry, and TT-611 tag. | Instrument engineer | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-10 | Confirm all "confirm" values in the setpoint list. | Client fire protection engineer | 2026-11-27 |
